reason: Rails advances a `Time` with `Time.now.utc.advance(seconds:)`; trails' `Time` analogue is `Temporal.Instant`, whose equivalent is `add({ milliseconds })`.

Rails formats the expiry with `Time#iso8601(3)`; `Temporal.Instant#toString({ smallestUnit: "millisecond" })` emits the identical millisecond-precision string (pinned by the Rails 7.0 fixtures in `message-verifier-metadata.test.ts`).
Rails parses with `Time.iso8601`; trails parses the same ISO 8601 string with `Temporal.Instant.from`.

`Time.parse` is Rails' non-ISO branch, reached only when `ActiveSupport.use_standard_json_time_format` is false; trails has no such setting, so only the ISO branch exists (story `activesupport-message-metadata-shared-suite`).
